title: state-machine-physics
intention: Make the node state-machine physics: the emit-chokepoint enforces the transition table over the state vocabulary (the -ME summons states; the PROVED / LEARNING rests), validates every workflow string against a known versioned node-class definition, and journals every transition and every workflow migration. The design lives in the MAP stone 'The node state-machine — states as summons'; this node is the work to turn that prose into enforcement (Law 4).
why: Today /sorted 'refuses illegal transitions' only as prose in the skill — an IOU. The vocabulary is ratified but not yet enforced; until the chokepoint enforces it, the refusal is policy, not physics. This node is where the vocabulary becomes the physics the whole ticket system runs on (state IS the pipeline instance). Cast self-hosting: the first node whose own `state` is written in the vocabulary it will enforce.
traces_to: Law 1 (state IS the pipeline instance — no re-derivation)
MAP 'The learning loop is the primitive'

falsifier.proves_green: proof gate (tester) — IOU. The proof a hollow build could not pass: construct a node whose workflow attempts an illegal transition and show the chokepoint refuses it; migrate a workflow by string-edit and show the journal crossing + version-validation; a driver whose method-pointer is unproven is refused (Law 8). Durability gate (code-seam): tested AND committed.
falsifier.proves_red: the vocabulary can't express a real node's lifecycle, OR a node arises needing a state/transition the vocabulary lacks, OR the -ME grammar rule mis-names a state (a summons with no -ME, or a node's-own-condition carrying one). Wrong-shape signal: if enforcing the transition table makes casting so rigid that real work routes around it, the table is wrong, not the work.
falsifier.horizon: first real enforcement — when the emit-chokepoint (base-class spine step) lands and the first node's transitions are gated by physics rather than the /sorted skill's prose.

(RESHAPED 2026-07-18 evening — SUPERSEDES the two entries above) A design conversation with Akien converged the runtime model and revealed the ground_loop-executor + scheduler-service code was the WRONG shape. The authoritative model is now `CairnCommons/intentions-not-beside-code/I-heartbeat-callbacks-and-bus.md`. Corrections that bear on THIS ticket: (1) the ground_loop is ONLY the HEARTBEAT (one daemon that beats) — it is not an executor; the run_driver logic was a goof. (2) Firing lives in the SHIM, not the ground loop: a device subscribes by a file in its tree, its shim fires the device's due CALLBACKS on each beat and STARTS the device (its own process) on demand. (3) CALLBACK (immutable, stateless, class-space) vs TICKET (mutable WORKFLOW node) are two species — LEARNING is a STATE, a callback is the WORKER a LEARNING node sets. (4) A trigger is ANYTHING THAT EVALUATES TO TRUE — the interval/date/quantity/state enum was a reification; evaluate where the data is OWNED (Law 6). (5) The BUS is the sole comm path (symmetric with db_domain=sole state path). The operational-driver primitive survives but is re-expressed in these terms; this ticket still WAITS ON the emit-chokepoint to enforce the state table.

RESHAPED 2026-08-05 — ruling 2026-08-05-gates-issue-clearances. THIS TICKET'S PREMISE CHANGED: the cursor is no longer the thing to make physics. A GATE ISSUES A CLEARANCE the way the tester issues a VALIDATION — one writer, append-only, address DERIVED from the ticket id (not a stored link, which would be a fourth record that can point somewhere wrong). Where a boat stands is DERIVED from its clearances and never written, so the ticket's state string DIES. Akien's motivation is the strongest argument: 'the workflow is inscribed on the ticket at creation time. it's order is not kept if it has to be sent back.' A linear path with a cursor cannot represent a voyage that went back; a dated sequence of grants and refusals loses nothing. AND THE CLASS DECLARES A PREREQUISITE GRAPH, NOT AN ORDER ('graph definitely') — which retires this ticket's back-edge-by-severity question outright: there is no 'how far back does a red throw you', only 'which prerequisite stopped being satisfied'.

[CORPUS] MEASURED 2026-08-05, AND IT IS THE EMPIRICAL CASE FOR THE ABOVE: state.json cursors carry SIXTEEN DISTINCT SHAPES across 27 components. Only 'at', 'seq' and 'standing' are universal; the rest vary (gate / from+to / build_gate / exit_gate / emission_gate / entry_gate / meter_reading / ratified_by / …). state.json is chartered as COMPILED FROM HISTORY AND NEVER HAND-EDITED — sixteen shapes says it is hand-written. That is the ticket-state defect one layer over, and it is what a record with no single writer always looks like. A clearance issued only by its gate has ONE shape by construction, because one writer means one schema. The measurement earns the ruling rather than the ruling being a preference (Law 3).

[CORPUS] WHAT SURVIVES OF THIS TICKET. history.json entries ALREADY carry a per-entry 'gate' field and are already append-only — so the clearance trail mostly exists and lacks only an OWNER on the append door. So the build is smaller than the ruling sounds: delete the ticket's state string, put an owner on the door, derive the trail address from the ticket id, and let state.json compile from what gates wrote. Everything else is already on disk.
